why: Both concern an attack's aftermath on the room's own mark, and the deciding line between fighting an attack and watching/repairing it is easily blurred when the concepts say 'defend' inside a maintenance theme.

why.T3-004: The concepts compare proposed images, versions and difficulty and settle the mark's look, which is T3-004's gate rather than T3-033's mere proposal or T3-070's directions.

why.T3-023: The whole sub is turned upside down for the day and members notice, explain and play inside the change, which is the takeover gate, not member fakes (T3-001) or official jokes (T3-048).

why.T3-054: The work is rebuilt on later canvases (PlaceTwo, the place rebootleg) rather than moved to a new spot on the same canvas (T3-022) or remade in another medium (T3-057).

why.T3-052: The bulk concerns the neighbouring figure/RTZ: naming it, proposing an 011 haircut on it, rejecting that, and ranking it against the logo, which is remarking on neighbouring pictures rather than settling a border (T3-010) or judging the canvas (T3-037).

why.T3-010: Seeking permission, asking to move, and agreeing boundaries at shared edges are the dominant act, so the border-settling gate leads; T3-011 (helping another room's work) and T3-024 (restraint by the room's own choice) are also at the floor and named in also_present.

why.T3-038: Counting the concepts, placing and reporting progress (started, coming together, lookin good, done) leads over explaining the event (T3-016, one), choosing a spot (T3-020, one) and announcing it is up (T3-026).

why.T3-029: The responses are grief for the lost Fred and Flintstar (silence, RIP, mark on history destroyed) rather than blame (T3-058) or the canvas's own end (T3-117).

why.T3-023: Same as position 2: the sub itself is turned upside down for April Fools and members play inside the change, so the takeover gate leads.

why.T3-021: The theme is declared maintenance: diagnosing damage, supplying the intended form and coordinates, explaining the five-minute repairs and reporting fixes. The 'defend' concepts ride inside this upkeep, so the watching-and-repairing gate leads over T3-005.

why.T3-017: This is ordinary side talk (a movie argument) drifting inside a canvas-related thread with no canvas work and no joke as its point, which is exactly T3-017's gate.

why.T3-117: The concepts register that the canvas event is over (coordinates too late, place ended, sad it's over, valiant effort), which is marking the canvas's end rather than mourning a single lost work (T3-029).

why.T3-009: The celebration of the finished work (the final product, praise, 'we did it', 'awesome job', survived to the end) holds the most concepts, so the finishing-celebration gate leads.
why.T3-043: Its own concepts thank the named organizer and designer and credit the organizing itself, which the celebration gate alone does not reach.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: Placing only T3-009 would carry the celebration of the final image but would drop the explicit thanks to /u/quadforce and /u/hika421 and the credit for the organizing, which are the theme's own doing.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0324841 thanks the organizer and designer and C0521343 credits the organizing effort, satisfying T3-043's gate of crediting who made the work.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-043: dropping it would lose only the credited thanks, while the celebration of the finished Stranger Place would remain.

why.T3-037: Welcoming the place evolving is a verdict on the canvas as a whole being worth doing, which is T3-037's gate rather than objecting to posts in a sub (T3-075) or spreading a colour (T3-171).

why.T3-014: The organizer sends questions and concerns to the room's Discord, moving part of the coordination into a chat, which is the moving-planning-into-a-chat gate.

why.T3-192: The letters are changed into a joke ('Stronger Things') and the changer jokingly claims points for it, which is griefing the work for fun and owning it, rather than a mistake owned (T3-170) or a call to attack a rival (T3-006).
